title: Test cases: HIP1R, and designed ENTH fusions (ENTH+AP180-IDP vs ENTH+albumin)

hip1r.interpretation: HIP1R straddles the Omega threshold (P=0.64): it has a strong extreme-N-terminal amphipathic moment (predicted ANTH wedge) plus 173 disordered residues, so unlike PICALM it can nearly reach productive curvature on its structural features -- but the prediction (does its N-terminus insert and tubulate?) needs experimental confirmation.

designed_fusions.rationale: Probe WHAT KIND of C-terminal partner rescues ENTH-domain curvature: a disordered brush (AP180 assembly domain) vs a folded globule (albumin) of comparable mass. curvo classifies each partner's disorder from its AlphaFold model (pLDDT + composition), so the crowding contribution is grounded, not assumed.
designed_fusions.verdict: A DISORDERED C-terminal partner rescues ENTH curvature; a FOLDED one does not. ENTH+AP180-IDP (c_eff 0.049) needs only 55 pN of actin force to reach Omega -- it behaves like, and slightly exceeds, full epsin (100 pN), because the AP180 assembly-domain brush substitutes for epsin's own crowding tail. ENTH+albumin (c_eff 0.010) is INDISTINGUISHABLE from ENTH-alone (both 175 pN): a folded globular cargo of comparable mass adds zero curvature drive. The mechanistic prediction: what you fuse to the ENTH C-terminus matters through its DISORDER (entropic brush crowding), not its presence or mass.
designed_fusions.caveat: Stage/threshold calls from the validated forward model. The crowding c_eff is CrowdingPlayer's Hill saturation with coverage set by the classifier's brush-residue count (idr/400 scaling, as in the family screen) -- a representation-level estimate, not a per-construct measurement. The folded-partner result rests on curvo's guardrail that a folded globule is not a polymer brush (0 brush residues), which is the physically correct call but should be confirmed by an in-vitro tubulation assay of the actual fusion.
